jobs.description: Employer: Oaklin Lane Expires: 09/22/2026 Project Management Intern — The Pediatric CollectiveLocation: RemotePosition Type: InternshipSchedule: Part-time during the academic year or full-time during the summerCompensation: PaidAbout The Pediatric CollectiveThe Pediatric Collective is an industry association. It brings together pediatric therapy companies, clinicians, parents, caregivers, researchers, and other industry leaders committed to improving access to high-quality care for children.Pediatric therapy does not receive enough attention despite the enormous need. Families often face long waitlists for speech, occupational, physical, and behavioral therapy—in some communities, children may wait months or even years for an appointment. jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Strategy & Operations Intern at Doc Wealth
jobs.description: Employer: Doc Wealth Expires: 09/24/2026 Strategy & Operations Intern (Year-Round, Path to Full-Time)We're building the largest physician-focused tax company in the country, growing faster than anyone in this space. This role sits inside the Founders Office, working directly with the COO on the problems that decide whether the firm wins: strategy, hiring, product, and the operating machinery underneath all of it. Read the whole post before applying.This is not an internship where you watch. You'll sit in the rooms where decisions get made, then own pieces of what comes out of them. One week that's building the model behind a pricing decision, the next it's running point on a search for a senior hire, the next it's turning a half-formed product idea into a spec someone can build. Real deadlines, real consequences, with someone experienced beside you and modern AI tooling at your back. The pace is fast and the standard is high. You'll learn more here in a few months than in a year anywhere else, because we hand you real responsibility and expect you to rise to it. Hard on purpose. If that sounds like too much, this is the wrong post.We need an absolute ninja. Someone who comes in, learns how the firm actually works, and earns the right to own bigger and bigger pieces of it.You'll doStrategy and analysisBuild the analyses behind real decisions: pricing changes, new service lines, pod capacity, which states and specialties to push into next.Pull data out of our systems, clean it, and turn it into a one-pager the COO can decide from. Numbers first, narrative second.Research competitors, markets, and tax industry shifts, and tell us what actually matters instead of dumping links.Pressure-test plans before they ship. Find the assumption that breaks, and say so.RecruitmentRun searches end to end for roles across the firm: write the post, source candidates, screen against our rubrics, schedule, keep the pipeline moving, and make sure no candidate is left hanging.Sit in on interviews, take structured notes, and build the debrief materials that drive the hire or no-hire call.Keep the Monday recruiting board clean and the funnel numbers honest.Product and internal toolingTurn dictated voice notes and whiteboard sessions into written specs, task lists, and process docs that an engineer or ops person can execute against.Test what gets built. Find where it breaks, document it precisely, and chase the fix until it closes.Help design and roll out the AI and automation workflows the firm runs on, so the team's reps go to judgment, not busywork.Founders Office operationsPrep leadership meetings: agenda, prior action items, the two or three numbers needed to run it.Capture action items out of leadership and pod meetings and chase them until they close, including with people more senior than you.Run special projects nobody owns yet: an offsite, a new vendor evaluation, a fire that landed on the COO's desk this morning.Draft communications the COO sends under their own name. They should need edits, not rewrites.Who this is forThe sharpest person in your program, and we mean that literally, because we require a 3.9+ overall GPA to apply. Learns fast, works hard without being told twice, energized by a heavy workload. Three things we care about most:Thinking. You can take an ambiguous question, structure it, do the work, and come back with a recommendation and the reasoning behind it. Not a summary of the problem. An answer.Communication. You write clean, professional messages and documents that people can act on without a rewrite. You follow up without being asked. You don't go quiet when something is stuck.Ownership and discretion. You'll see strategy before it's announced, comp, and personnel matters. That information does not leave your hands. When something is yours, it gets done or you raise your hand early. Nothing dies silently in your queue.And be honest with yourself about the unglamorous work. Founders Office means you do whatever the firm needs, and some of it is scheduling, data cleanup, and chasing people for the same document three times. It still has to be right, because everything downstream depends on it. If work below your ego drains you, this is not the right seat.This is not for anyone who needs hand-holding or wants a comfortable lane.Boundary on scope: you'll prepare the analysis and the options. Decisions with real legal or financial exposure belong to the COO and the founders. You will never be left holding those alone.The path: Perform and you convert to full-time in the Founders Office, then keep climbing. Earned, not given.Selection: We screen hard. Very few who apply are selected. If you're the right person, that should make you want this more.Details$14 to $20 an hour, 30 to 40 hours per week.Fully remote.Year-round, running through until you graduate.RequirementsGraduating May 2027 or later.Minimum 3.9 overall GPA. We will verify. If you're below it, please don't apply.Pursuing a degree in business, finance, accounting, economics, or a related program. Exceptional candidates from other fields will be considered.Strong written communication. Be ready to show a writing sample or write something on the spot.Comfortable in spreadsheets, fast with new software, and already using AI tools in your own work.Discretion with confidential information, without needing to be reminded.Hungry to earn a full-time seat and own it.

They get discharged from the hospital with no follow-up plan. They miss medications because nobody explained the instructions. They give up trying to fight a denied insurance claim. They don't know what they're entitled to, and there's nobody helping them figure it out. The system wasn't built for them, it was built around them.Pinnie Health exists to fix that. We're building the first AI-powered care advocacy platform that gives every older adult on Medicare a dedicated human advocate, backed by AI that handles the research, coordination, and follow-up, at zero cost to the patient. We launched three months ago, we've already enrolled over 100 patients, we're licensed in 46 states, and we're growing fast. This is early-stage, high-impact work at the intersection of healthcare and technology, and we're just getting started. The RoleWe're looking for someone who understands how to build a social media presence from nothing. Someone who's already grown accounts on Instagram, Facebook, or both, and can prove it. You'll be our first dedicated social media hire. The job is building Pinnie's organic presence across Instagram and Facebook from scratch: daily content using a mix of AI-generated visuals, static graphics, patient testimonials, short-form video, articles, community posts, and whatever formats you think will connect with our audience. You'll also help manage a UGC agency we're working with to produce creator content around elder care and Medicare. The people you'll be making content for are older adults navigating Medicare, dealing with denied claims, trying to find a doctor who actually listens. The audience is their families, their caregivers, and the patients themselves. There are 67 million people on Medicare in this country, and almost nobody is making good content for them. That's the opportunity. We're not handing you a content calendar and asking you to execute. We want someone entrepreneurial who will come in, take ownership, and treat this like their own brand. You'll work directly with both founders, you'll have budget to spend, and you'll have the freedom to move fast. If you prove you can grow it, this becomes a full-time role. What You'll DoBuild and run our Instagram and Facebook. Create and publish content daily across both platforms. Static posts, carousels, Reels, Stories, testimonials, AI-generated imagery, quote cards, articles, community discussion posts. You'll figure out what formats work on each platform and double down on what gets traction. Use AI tools to move fast. You're comfortable with tools like Midjourney, ChatGPT, Higgsfield, or whatever's new this week. You use them to produce more and better content, not as a crutch. Grow an organic community. Build a following of Medicare beneficiaries, their adult children, and caregivers who actually engage. We care about people who click through and sign up, not vanity follower counts. Figure out what content sparks conversation and sharing in this audience. Manage our UGC agency. We're working with a UGC agency to produce creator content. You'll be the point person: reviewing briefs, giving feedback on deliverables, making sure the output fits our brand and actually performs. Experiment constantly. Test hooks, formats, posting times, hashtag strategies, content series. Track what works. Kill what doesn't. Bring us ideas we haven't thought of. Why PinnieYou'll build a brand for a massive underserved audience. 67 million Medicare beneficiaries. Their adult children. Their caregivers. Nobody is making great social content for this population. You get to own that space. We'll give you real ownership. No approval chains, no brand police. If you have an idea, pitch it at standup and post it that afternoon. We're a small team that moves fast, and we'll back you if you show results. The content matters. This isn't promoting a lifestyle brand or selling SaaS. The stories you'll tell are about real people getting help they couldn't find anywhere else. Families find us through the content you'll create. It can turn into a career. This starts as a part-time role. If you grow the channels and prove you can own the function, we'll convert it to full-time. Who You AreYou've grown a social media account and can show the numbers. Yours, a brand's, a client's. We want to see the before and after.You think big and are entrepreneurial. We want to take big swings and build a massive brand to drive awareness about a service that matters. You post consistently. Not once a week. Daily or close to it. You understand that cadence is half the game.You're fluent in AI content tools. You already use them in your workflow and can show us what you've made with them.You have visual taste. Your feed doesn't look like a template dump. You know color, composition, and typography well enough to make things people want to share.You can write captions and short copy that sounds human, not like a brand account. No "we're thrilled to announce." Real voice.Based in or near NYC. Some in-person collaboration in our Tribeca office, but most of the work is remote. What You Don't NeedA marketing degreeAgency experienceA follower countWe care about what you can make, not what's on your resume. DetailsLocation: Remote (If in NYC, hybrid as needed in our Tribeca office)Hours: ~20 hrs/week, flexible scheduleCompensation: Hourly Paid Internship ($ based on experience)Duration: 3 months with potential to extend or convert How to Apply1. Please submit your resume on this job post.2. Please go to pinnie.com and spend some time understanding what we do and who we serve. Then email aashay@pinnie.com the following: a. An account you've grown. Include the handle and the numbers (where it started, where it is now, timeframe). b. A content plan. We're starting from zero on Instagram and Facebook. Pitch us 2-3 content series or recurring formats you'd launch in your first two weeks. Tell us why you think they'd work for this audience. c. One big idea. What would you do in the first 90 days to build a real community around Pinnie? We're not looking for a polished deck. A few paragraphs showing how you think is plenty. That's the whole application.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Founders Office Intern at Doc Wealth
jobs.description: Employer: Doc Wealth Expires: 09/24/2026 Founders Office Intern (Year-Round, Path to Full-Time)We're building the largest physician-focused tax company in the country, growing faster than anyone in this space. This role sits inside the Founders Office, working directly with the COO on the problems that decide whether the firm wins: strategy, hiring, product, and the operating machinery underneath all of it. Read the whole post before applying.This is not an internship where you watch. You'll sit in the rooms where decisions get made, then own pieces of what comes out of them. One week that's building the model behind a pricing decision, the next it's running point on a search for a senior hire, the next it's turning a half-formed product idea into a spec someone can build. Real deadlines, real consequences, with someone experienced beside you and modern AI tooling at your back. The pace is fast and the standard is high. You'll learn more here in a few months than in a year anywhere else, because we hand you real responsibility and expect you to rise to it. Hard on purpose. If that sounds like too much, this is the wrong post.We need an absolute ninja. Someone who comes in, learns how the firm actually works, and earns the right to own bigger and bigger pieces of it.You'll doStrategy and analysisBuild the analyses behind real decisions: pricing changes, new service lines, pod capacity, which states and specialties to push into next.Pull data out of our systems, clean it, and turn it into a one-pager the COO can decide from. Numbers first, narrative second.Research competitors, markets, and tax industry shifts, and tell us what actually matters instead of dumping links.Pressure-test plans before they ship. Find the assumption that breaks, and say so.RecruitmentRun searches end to end for roles across the firm: write the post, source candidates, screen against our rubrics, schedule, keep the pipeline moving, and make sure no candidate is left hanging.Sit in on interviews, take structured notes, and build the debrief materials that drive the hire or no-hire call.Keep the Monday recruiting board clean and the funnel numbers honest.Product and internal toolingTurn dictated voice notes and whiteboard sessions into written specs, task lists, and process docs that an engineer or ops person can execute against.Test what gets built. Find where it breaks, document it precisely, and chase the fix until it closes.Help design and roll out the AI and automation workflows the firm runs on, so the team's reps go to judgment, not busywork.Founders Office operationsPrep leadership meetings: agenda, prior action items, the two or three numbers needed to run it.Capture action items out of leadership and pod meetings and chase them until they close, including with people more senior than you.Run special projects nobody owns yet: an offsite, a new vendor evaluation, a fire that landed on the COO's desk this morning.Draft communications the COO sends under their own name. They should need edits, not rewrites.Who this is forThe sharpest person in your program, and we mean that literally, because we require a 3.9+ overall GPA to apply. Learns fast, works hard without being told twice, energized by a heavy workload. Three things we care about most:Thinking. You can take an ambiguous question, structure it, do the work, and come back with a recommendation and the reasoning behind it. Not a summary of the problem. An answer.Communication. You write clean, professional messages and documents that people can act on without a rewrite. You follow up without being asked. You don't go quiet when something is stuck.Ownership and discretion. You'll see strategy before it's announced, comp, and personnel matters. That information does not leave your hands. When something is yours, it gets done or you raise your hand early. Nothing dies silently in your queue.And be honest with yourself about the unglamorous work. Founders Office means you do whatever the firm needs, and some of it is scheduling, data cleanup, and chasing people for the same document three times. It still has to be right, because everything downstream depends on it. If work below your ego drains you, this is not the right seat.This is not for anyone who needs hand-holding or wants a comfortable lane.Boundary on scope: you'll prepare the analysis and the options. Decisions with real legal or financial exposure belong to the COO and the founders. You will never be left holding those alone.The path: Perform and you convert to full-time in the Founders Office, then keep climbing. Earned, not given.Selection: We screen hard. Very few who apply are selected. If you're the right person, that should make you want this more.Details$14 to $20 an hour, 30 to 40 hours per week.Fully remote.Year-round, running through until you graduate.RequirementsGraduating May 2027 or later.Minimum 3.9 overall GPA. We will verify. If you're below it, please don't apply.Pursuing a degree in business, finance, accounting, economics, or a related program. Exceptional candidates from other fields will be considered.Strong written communication. Be ready to show a writing sample or write something on the spot.Comfortable in spreadsheets, fast with new software, and already using AI tools in your own work.Discretion with confidential information, without needing to be reminded.Hungry to earn a full-time seat and own it.

These projects could include exposure, within our sales division, across various segments including targeted development in these areas: Dealer Enablement: Dealer Trainings & Development, Owner Connections, Fixed Operations, Low Funnel Marketing. Business Development & Channel: Dealer Policies, Dealer Distribution Footprint, Key Market Performance Management, Showroom Display & Merchandising. Product Line Sales: Program Development & Execution, Demand/Supply Analytics, Competitive Analysis, Retail Critical Thinking Leadership. Field Sales: Dealership Experience, Retail Root Cause & Countermeasure, Dealer Operations Improvement, Solicitation Ownership, Sales Enablement. We encourage you to embrace the adventure and be open to any placement opportunity. Being mobile and flexible will allow you to gain diverse experiences and make the most of your internship. Internship Locations Could Include: Plymouth, MN or Medina, MN. This program serves as a primary feeder into our rotational leadership development program, providing you as an intern with the foundational skills and experiences needed to excel in your career. Upon completion of the internship program, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a passion to learn may be offered a returning internship or a full-time position, depending on eligibility. As a Polaris intern it is important that you embrace the adventure and remain open to any placement opportunity. By being adaptable, you will gain diverse experiences and develop a broader skill set, which are essential for your professional development and success within Polaris. Our internship program is crafted to build the foundational skills and experiences essential for your career success. Upon completing the internship, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a strong passion for learning may be offered a returning internship or a position in our rotational leadership development program. Programming Hours: weekly functional and centralized learning sessions to broaden your knowledge base, both within and beyond your program. Networking: intentional time with peers and leaders at Polaris to build your professional network. Early Talent Summit Week: you participate in our 3-day event in our Wyoming, MN office. All specific internship assignments are communicated in February, after aligning based on your specific interests and business demand. To qualify for these services your home address must be 35 miles or more from the office where you will be working. Your responsibilities will include daily transportation to/from the office. Required Qualifications: Pursuing a bachelor’s/master’s degree in business with an emphasis in Sales, Marketing, or other related degree with an intended graduation date between August 2027-May 2029. Minimum overall GPA of 3.0 Must be able to commit to a full 12-week internship, working 40 hours per week, within one of the following date ranges: May 17th – August 6th, 2027. June 1st – August 20th, 2027. Willing and able to relocate. Demonstrated strengths in analysis, creative problem-solving, communication, interpersonal relationships, self-motivation, and leadership. jobs.description: Employer: Polaris Inc. Expires: 09/24/2026 Marketing Internship - Summer 2027 Company Overview Polaris Inc. is a global leader in powersports and known to millions of people around the world as we offer a diverse portfolio of products and services including boats, off-road vehicles, commercial vehicles, and more. Polaris pioneers’ product breakthroughs and enriching experiences and services, that have invited people to discover the joy of being outdoors since our founding in 1954. At Polaris, we have fun doing what we love by driving change and innovation. We empower employees to take on challenging assignments and roles with an elevated level of responsibility in our agile working environment. Our people make us who we are and help create incredible products and experiences that empower us to Think Outside. Internship Program Overview The Polaris Marketing Internship (MIP) is a tailored 12-week paid summer internship designed for emerging sophomores, juniors, and seniors who are interested in pursuing a career in a leading global powersports industry. As a Marketing Intern, you will be given impactful project-based assignments that directly align with business objectives. These projects could include exposure, within our marketing division, across various segments including targeted development in these areas: Brand and Product Marketing (Brand/Lifestyle Marketing, Insights and Analytics) How you create and capture through brand and product marketing Creative and Content (Social Media, Paid Media, Partnerships, Events) How Creative and Content Creation drives business today and tomorrow Process and Go-to-Market (Ecommerce, Digital Production) How Process, Planning and communication improve work Dealer and Channel (Channel, Retail, Owner Experience, In-Market and Key Market Impact) How Dealership and Sales Channels impact our business We encourage you to embrace the adventure and be open to any placement opportunity. Being mobile and flexible will allow you to gain diverse experiences and make the most of your internship. Internship Locations Could Include: Any Polaris location across the United States. This program serves as a primary feeder into our rotational leadership development program, providing you as an intern with the foundational skills and experiences needed to excel in your career. Upon completion of the internship program, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a passion to learn may be offered a returning internship or a full-time position, depending on eligibility. As a Polaris intern it is important that you embrace the adventure and remain open to any placement opportunity. By being adaptable, you will gain diverse experiences and develop a broader skill set, which are essential for your professional development and success within Polaris. Our internship program is crafted to build the foundational skills and experiences essential for your career success. Upon completing the internship, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a strong passion for learning may be offered a returning internship or a position in our rotational leadership development program. In addition to meaningful project work, you will participate in intentional programming and professional development offerings such as: Mentorship: you are paired with one of our DP associates for mentor support throughout your 12-weeks. Programming Hours: weekly functional and centralized learning sessions to broaden your knowledge base, both within and beyond your program. Networking: intentional time with peers and leaders at Polaris to build your professional network. Intern Innovation Challenge: internal case study designed to promote cross functional development where you and your team will present creative and practical solutions to a real ‘Polaris’ problem to our executive leadership. Early Talent Summit Week: you participate in our 3-day event in our Wyoming, MN office. This immersive experience brings together all US interns and DPs for professional development, structured networking, a DP graduation event, inspiring executive speakers, and a thrilling team ride on some of your favorite Polaris vehicles. Community Engagement: opportunity to get involved in your local community. Final Presentations: present to our senior level leaders to showcase your career aspirations and recap your internship experience. The Selection Process: Applications are open from August -November each year. Applications will be reviewed and shortlisted candidates will typically be contacted for an initial phone screen by the end of November. Candidates selected to move forward will be invited to participate in a virtual panel interview with an identified HR business partner and functional leader. Successful candidates would move forward to an offer. You will partner with the Early Talent team in January to complete a survey that provides a deeper look at your specific interests, strengths & career goals. All specific internship assignments are communicated in February, after aligning based on your specific interests and business demand. Intern Relocation Assistance: Polaris offers a relocation program for interns who qualify through our mobility vendor. To qualify for these services, your home address must be 35 miles or more from the office where you will be working. Benefits include a lump sum (grossed up to offset tax liability), access to a relocation counselor to explain the resources available to you and aid in securing short-term housing available to you. Your responsibilities will include daily transportation to/from the office. Required Qualifications: Pursuing a bachelor’s/ master’s degree in Marketing, Strategic Communications, or other related business degree with an emphasis in Marketing with an intended graduation date between August 2027-May 2029. Minimum overall GPA of 3.0 Must be able to commit to a full 12-week internship, working 40 hours per week, within one of the following date ranges: May 17th – August 6th, 2027. June 1st – August 20th, 2027. Willing and able to relocate. Must be a U.S. person (U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident, asylee, or refugee) and not require sponsorship for employment now or in the future. Must have reliable transportation for daily commuting to and from the office. Previous experience with Microsoft Office software tools (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams, and Word). Preferred Qualifications: Previous Internship/Co-op experience or involvement in relevant projects. Demonstrated strengths in analysis, creative problem-solving, communication, interpersonal relationships, self-motivation, and leadership. Strong interest in long-term career development and participation in leadership development programs. Previous leadership experience in work, organizations, or classroom. Completion of at least two years of university coursework Strong Communication (both written and verbal including strong presentation skills) Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, ever-changing, multi-tasking environment Strong organizational and project management skills This is more than an internship - It's the beginning of your career with Polaris. We hope you're ready for the ultimate adventure!

jobs.title: Marketing Intern at Peak Retirement Planning, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Peak Retirement Planning, Inc. Expires: 09/24/2026 We are the #1 fastest-growing private company in Columbus, Ohio, by Inc. 5000, and one of the top and youngest financial planning firms in the country. Peak has grown from one team member to over 60 team members in just 4 years. In 2025, we had over 5,400 applicants, we only hired 19. As a scaling start-up, we are very particular to ensure we hire the best and those aligned with our values and intensity. We are not a firm for everyone. At Peak, we integrate Christian and conservative values and biblical principles in everything we do. Earning an internship at Peak is a HUGE honor. We had over 1,000 interns apply in 2025 and selected only 20, so if you are chosen, you have been carefully selected. Our internship program is highly competitive and the top in the country. We have opportunities for summer, fall, and spring internships. Why do we do internships? 1. Hire Future Team Members - Hiring is our number one bottleneck with the extreme momentum and growth our firm has experienced. This gives us an opportunity to find and test great-fit future team members before offering full-time. Our goal is to offer back every intern who crushes it and aligns with our values/standards/intensity. 2. Impact - Interns don't add much value to us during the internship. We can get all the tasks done with 5 interns. This is a mission to pour into interns. It is a Professional Development Masterclass and an incredible opportunity to grow in all areas of life. Few firms offer robust internship programs, so we decided to change that and build it ourselves. What We Offer🚀 Real life Experience – We have 13 Marketing Funnels and some of the best marketing in the financial planning industry. Help maximize them through tasks and projects while working closely with our Marketing team. Top Compensation – Most of our interns make all-in $20-30 an hour (not including the up to $10k signing bonus opportunity for those offered back). Peak University - Our three-month advisor training program, consisting of one-hour of training sessions every day with an experienced advisor. Marketing interns get to sit in on some of these classes. Peak Bootcamp - Leadership and Professional Development masterclass held every day for the first month. Intern Bootcamp - An additional hour each day for interns to have time with experienced team members to get questions answered and do further training. CEO Fridays – A time when our CEO will discuss mission, values, firm alignment, firm direction, industry experience, advice to interns, answer questions, and anything related to Peak. Intern Lunches - For interns who are excelling, have a great attitude, and show the qualities of a long-term team member, we host one-on-one lunches with our experienced team members throughout the summer. Growth Sessions - One-on-one intentional discussions with leaders of our internship program to help interns grow. Kingdom Advisors Study Group - Learn how to integrate your faith with your finances. Trainual - Over 120+ hours of training content built exclusively for Peak Retirement Planning, Inc. Top Dog Day - Those we offer back and accept will be invited to a special full-day experience of a lifetime. We will have the whole day planned, with top restaurant reservations in Columbus for breakfast/lunch/dinner. We will plan special activities such as golfing, skydiving, rock climbing, escape rooms, etc. Team Events - We have Peak Olympics, Team Dinners, Columbus Crew Games, Columbus Clippers Games, and more throughout the summer! Out-of-State Interns: Paid for housing during the internship.

Expires: 09/24/2026 As a project intern, you will have the opportunity to engage in impactful short-term projects that provide you with a glimpse of professional real-world experience. You will gain practical skills through on-the-job learning in a fast-paced work environment and develop a deeper understanding of your career interests.Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage you to apply early.Successful candidates must be able to commit to at least 3 months long internship period.TikTok Shop is an innovative new commerce platform that is redefining the way people discover and shop online. Through seamless in-app shopping experiences, we enable sellers, creators, and communities to drive real commercial value.Are you eager to gain hands-on experience in business development, influencer marketing, and e-commerce? Want to work on real projects that drive impact? At TikTok Shop, we’re reshaping how brands connect with creators and consumers—and this is your chance to be part of it!As an intern you’ll be directly involved in identifying top brands, supporting partnerships, and optimizing campaign execution. You won’t be fetching coffee—you’ll be making a difference.About the team: The TikTok Shop Europe Business Planning & Operations (BP&O) team focuses on developing e-commerce strategies for emerging markets. We drive market growth by crafting tailored plans, optimising operations, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to support merchants and creators. Our mission is to enable sustainable success in Europe's dynamic e-commerce landscape through data-driven insights and innovative solutions.This is a highly unique role that combines both strategy and execution, helping support TikTok Shop's start-up growth in the rapidly scaling Spanish market. As a project intern, you will work cross-functionally and independently to analyse data, uncover opportunities, design initiatives, and help launch them in the market to generate real business impact. You will gain practical skills through on-the-job learning in a fast-paced environment and develop a deeper understanding of your career interests.Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis; we encourage you to apply early. Successful candidates must be able to commit to an internship of at least 3 months, on-site 5 days per week.ResponsibilitiesData & Analysis: Gather internal and external data and produce in-depth, data-driven analyses of the e-commerce business, covering merchant growth, product and content scaling, and other key metrics.Monitoring & Diagnosis: Build and maintain business analysis frameworks and trackers to monitor key indicators, surface opportunities and risks, and translate findings into practical solutions.Cross-functional Execution: Coordinate with account management, marketing, category, logistics, and product teams to drive short-term and long-term initiatives to landing.Operational Support: Maintain operational documentation, weekly meeting materials, and SOPs, and support merchant and creator communications and feedback collection. QualificationsMinimum QualificationsCurrently enrolled in a Bachelor's degree or above in Business Analytics, Economics, Statistics, Data Science, Finance, or a related field.Fluent in Chinese to work effectively with internal teams based in Mainland China, and fluent in English to collaborate with local stakeholders across Europe.Working proficiency in Spanish to communicate with local merchants, creators, and market partners in Spain.Strong data analysis skills with structured, logical thinking.Fast, sharp and proactive learner, able to self-learn, explore independently, and ask the right questions.Strong multitasking ability, with clear prioritisation in a fast-paced environment.Clear and fluent communicator, able to drive cross-functional initiatives to completion.Preferred QualificationsConsulting, strategy, or investment-related experience is a plus.Interest in social commerce, content-driven e-commerce, or digital advertising.Job InformationAbout TikTok TikTok is the leading destination for short-form mobile video. Our innovative product is built to help people authentically express themselves, discover and connect – and our global, diverse teams make that possible. Together, we create value for our communities, inspire creativity and bring joy - a mission we work towards every day.We strive to do great things with great people. We lead with curiosity, humility, and a desire to make impact in a rapidly growing tech company. Every challenge is an opportunity to learn and innovate as one team. Join us.Diversity & Inclusion TikTok is committed to creating an inclusive space where employees are valued for their skills, experiences, and unique perspectives. Our platform connects people from across the globe and so does our workplace. At TikTok, our mission is to inspire creativity and bring joy. To achieve that goal, we are committed to celebrating our diverse voices and to creating an environment that reflects the many communities we reach. We are passionate about this and hope you are too.

jobs.description: Employer: Morgan Stanley Expires: 09/25/2026 To be considered for this program you must apply on the Morgan Stanley website: https://morganstanley.tal.net/vx/brand-0/spa-1/candidate/so/pm/1/pl/1/opp/20887-2027-Corporate-Treasury-Summer-Analyst-Program-New-York/en-GBEducation Level: Bachelor's Degree Morgan Stanley is a leading global financial services firm providing a wide range of investment banking, securities, investment management and wealth management services. The Firm's employees serve clients worldwide including corporations, governments, and individuals from more than 1,200 offices in 43 countries. As a market leader, the talent and passion of our people is critical to our success. Together, we share a common set of values rooted in integrity, excellence, and strong team ethic. Morgan Stanley can provide a superior foundation for building a professional career a place for people to learn, achieve and grow. A philosophy that balances personal lifestyles, perspectives and needs is an important part of our culture. Summer Analysts join the firm for 10 weeks in June and are placed on a team within the Corporate Treasury and Capital Planning department. They will receive in-depth exposure to a specific Corporate Treasury or Capital Planning team, while gaining a broader understanding of the Corporate Treasury and Capital Planning and its various functions. CORPORATE TREASURY AND CAPITAL PLANNING Corporate Treasury and Capital Planning provide corporate finance advisory service to senior management and internal business units. They also optimize the Firm’s liquidity and capital base, manages the Firm’s foreign exchange and interest rate exposure, and coordinates relationships with regulators.. TRAINING PROGRAM The Summer Analyst Program begins with Firmwide, Finance, Corporate Treasury and Capital Planning specific training in which Analysts are immersed in the culture and atmosphere of Morgan Stanley while also being taught core skills essential for successful completion of the Program. Summer Analysts will receive support from a Direct Manager and Peer Mentor, as well as opportunities to network with peers, and Senior Management through team-building sessions, community service and other organized events. ROLE AND RESPONSIBILITIES Assist in the reporting and analysis of the Firm's funding, liquidity and capital profile. Collaborate with teams to assist in performing stress testing, scenario planning and analysis, and peer benchmarking. Partner with stakeholders to identify and implement process optimization strategies that enhance the effectiveness of monitoring capital, liquidity or funding activities Analyze regulatory changes and their impact on the Firm’s business processes. Apply through the Grant Thornton Job portal at www.grantthornton.com/campuscareers (including resume and transcript) Who is Grant Thornton? At Grant Thornton, we believe in making business more personal and building trust into every result – for our clients and you. Here, we go beyond your expectations of a career in professional services by offering a career path with more: more opportunity, more flexibility, and more support. It’s what makes us different, and we think being different makes us better. In the U.S., Grant Thornton delivers professional services through two specialized entities: Grant Thornton LLP, a licensed, certified public accounting (CPA) firm that provides audit and assurance services ― and Grant Thornton Advisors LLC (not a licensed CPA firm), which exclusively provides non-attest offerings, including tax and advisory services. In 2025, Grant Thornton formed a multinational, multidisciplinary platform with Grant Thornton Ireland. The platform offers a premier Trans-Atlantic advisory and tax practice, as well as independent American and Irish audit practices. With $2.7 billion in revenues and more than 50 offices spanning the U.S., Ireland and other territories, the platform delivers a singular client experience that includes enhanced solutions and capabilities, backed by powerful technologies and a roster of 12,000 quality-driven professionals enjoying exceptional career-growth opportunities and a distinctive cross-border culture. Our advisory practice creates holistic solutions delivered by innovative, curious professionals who bring technical depth and industry insight to our clients. What is Risk Advisory? Within our Cyber & Risk Solution Family, Risk Advisory helps organizations grow with confidence by delivering agile, technology-enabled risk services that strengthen resilience, improve business performance, and unlock new opportunities. We work with complex organizations to assess, transform, and operate internal controls, risk management, compliance and Internal Audit activities, programs, and functions. jobs.title: Tax Intern - Winter 2027 - Reno at Grant Thornton
jobs.description: Employer: Grant Thornton Expires: 09/25/2026 Please apply to the one position/location you are most interested in. In order to be considered for this position, you must apply through the Grant Thornton Job portal at www.grantthornton.com/careers (including resume and transcript). Who is Grant Thornton? At Grant Thornton, we believe in making business more personal and building trust into every result – for our clients and you. Here, we go beyond your expectations of a career in professional services by offering a career path with more: more opportunity, more flexibility, and more support. It’s what makes us different, and we think being different makes us better. In the U.S., Grant Thornton delivers professional services through two specialized entities: Grant Thornton LLP, a licensed, certified public accounting (CPA) firm that provides audit and assurance services ― and Grant Thornton Advisors LLC (not a licensed CPA firm), which exclusively provides non-attest offerings, including tax and advisory services. In 2025, Grant Thornton formed a multinational, multidisciplinary platform with Grant Thornton Ireland. The platform offers a premier Trans-Atlantic advisory and tax practice, as well as independent American and Irish audit practices. With $2.7 billion in revenues and more than 50 offices spanning the U.S., Ireland and other territories, the platform delivers a singular client experience that includes enhanced solutions and capabilities, backed by powerful technologies and a roster of 12,000 quality-driven professionals enjoying exceptional career-growth opportunities and a distinctive cross-border culture. Grant Thornton is part of the Grant Thornton International Limited network, which provides access to its member firms in more than 150 global markets. What is Tax? Grant Thornton's tax specialists complement our clients’ accounting teams while maintaining their auditors' independence with our compliance services and customized tax planning advice. We have capabilities to advise our clients on various tax strategies including federal tax services, state and local tax services, international tax services, industry tax services, family wealth planning, and compensation and benefit plan design, as well as consult on other complex tax matters. Why become a Tax Intern at Grant Thornton? During your internship at Grant Thornton, you will be exposed to tax procedures including tax consulting and tax return preparation which will involve tax research, tax planning, and the preparation of supporting work papers on various tax returns and projects. You will have an opportunity to work alongside Partners, Senior Executives, and peers as a member of the engagement team. Additionally, you will have an opportunity to learn new skillsets, be involved in office community activities, and build lasting relationships with members of the Grant Thornton team. Your internship will include, but will not be limited to, the following: Working on a variety of client engagements in varying industries. Networking with your peers. Meeting with your mentor for regular feedback and professional development discussions. Connecting with fellow interns and Grant Thornton staff at social events. Participating in team-building exercises. Giving back to the community through outreach activities. Sharpening your leadership skills. Additional Job Responsibilities Include Reviewing data input, identifying and resolving technical tax issues, and assisting in the review of tax preparations completed by our colleagues in Bangalore, India. Responding to inquiries from the IRS and other taxing authorities. Identifying, researching, and assessing various tax issues while also providing information to senior staff members. Identifying and carrying out other projects as assigned. Collaboratively working with client team members while building rapport and strong client relationships. Networking with your peers. Meeting with your mentor for regular feedback and professional development discussions. Connecting with fellow interns and Grant Thornton staff at social events. Participating in team-building exercises. Giving back to the community through outreach activities. Sharpening your leadership skills. Other duties as assigned. Qualifications Pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Accounting. Minimum major and overall GPA of 3.0/4.0 preferred. The willingness and ability to work additional hours, as needed, and travel to various client sites. Excellent analytical, communication (written and verbal), and interpersonal skills. Strong technical aptitude and skillset. Demonstrated project management skillset including project planning and time management Ability to work efficiently and effectively in a complex team environment. Ability to travel on short notice and work additional hours as necessary. Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future. No visa sponsorship is available for this position. The team you’re about to join is ready to help you thrive. Here’s how: Whether it’s your work location, weekly schedule or flex time off, we empower you with the options to work in the way that best serves your clients and your life. Consistent with the firm’s hybrid work model, this position will require in-person attendance at least three days per week, either at a GT office or client site. Here, you are supported to prioritize your overall well-being through work-life integration options that work best for you and those in your household. We understand that your needs, responsibilities and experiences are different — and we think that’s a good thing. That’s why we support you with personalized and comprehensive benefits that recognize and empower all the identities, roles and aspirations that make you, well, you. See how at www.gt.com/careers. When it comes to inclusion, we are committed to doing more than checking boxes. Explore all the ways we’re taking action for diversity, equity & inclusion at www.gt.com/careers. Here’s what you can expect next: If you apply and are selected to interview, a Grant Thornton team member will reach out to you to schedule a time to connect. We encourage you to also check out other roles that may be a good fit for you or get to know us a little bit better at www.gt.com/careers. Benefits: We understand that your needs, responsibilities and experiences are different, and we think that’s a good thing. That’s why we support you with personalized and comprehensive benefits that recognize and empower all the identities, roles and aspirations that make you, well, you. For an overview of our benefit offerings, please visit: https://www.grantthornton.com/careers/rewards-and-benefits. Benefits for internship positions: Grant Thornton interns are eligible to participate in the firm’s medical, dental and vision insurance programs and the firm’s employee assistance program. Interns also receive a minimum of 72 hours of paid sick leave, and are paid for firm holidays that fall within their internship period. Benefits for seasonal employee positions: Grant Thornton seasonal employees are eligible to participate in the firm’s medical, dental and vision insurance programs and the firm’s employee assistance program. Seasonal employees may also be eligible to participate in the firm’s 401(k) savings plan and employee retirement plan in accordance with applicable plan terms and eligibility requirements. Seasonal employees receive a minimum of 72 hours of paid sick leave. Grant Thornton employees may be eligible for a discretionary, annual bonus based on individual and firm performance, subject to the terms, conditions and eligibility criteria of the applicable bonus plan or program. Interns and seasonal employees are not eligible for bonus compensation. Additional Details: It is the policy of Grant Thornton to promote equal employment opportunities. All personnel decisions (including, but not limited to, recruiting, hiring, training, working conditions, promotion, transfer, compensation, benefits, evaluations, and termination) are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, marital or civil union status, pregnancy or pregnancy-related condition, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, citizenship status, veteran status, disability, handicap, genetic predisposition or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. Consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and applicable state and local laws, it is the policy of Grant Thornton to provide reasonable accommodation when requested by a qualified applicant or employee with a disability, unless such accommodation would cause an undue hardship. The policy regarding requests for reasonable accommodation applies to all aspects of employment, including the application process. To make an accommodation request, please contact HR@us.gt.com. For Los Angeles Applicants only: We will consider for employment all qualified Applicants, including those with Criminal Histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.
